## Context

Part of **Mini-Boss rewards become valuable (AH-0MVLISU03006WDOD)**. The
paired implementation item for "Test the mini-boss wheel overlay and spin
behaviour": this item makes those tests green.

## Summary

New launcher-agnostic wheel overlay scene `src/scenes/MiniBossWheelScene.ts`
mirroring `MineralChoiceScene`'s overlay pattern (pause, single optional
result callback, demo auto-select contract). The scene receives the owned-kind
wedges and a resolved outcome from the launcher; it only animates and reports,
never computes probabilities.

## Design

- Registered in `src/core/gameConfig.ts` so `scene.launch('MiniBossWheelScene',
  …)` works everywhere.
- Payload: `wedges` (one per owned permanent kind + bonus wedge, each carrying
  the code-drawn icon + display name), `outcome` (target wedge index + extra
  gained wedges for multi-upgrade spins), optional `onResult` callback
  (mirrors `MineralChoiceScene.onSelect`), and optional `autoSpinMs`
  (demo mode: after `BOT_MINERAL_CHOICE_DELAY_MS`) / `fireSchedule` (reduced-
  volume ghost fire while paused, reusing the shared hold-full metronome).
- Spin: pointer click or any keyboard key starts a fast-start, ease-out
  rotation (≈2.2 s total, at most one overshoot revolution, duration exported
  as a constant) that stops on the target wedge; the landed wedge is
  highlighted; the result callback fires exactly once; a later spin is a
  no-op.
- **Multi-upgrade reveal (producer answer Q2):** when the outcome grants 2–3
  kinds, the landing wedge renders **all** the gained kinds' icons inside that
  one wedge ("all icons present") — the other gained kinds are not lit up on
  separate wedges — so the complete result is legible at the pointer.
- Tension over predictability: the wedge list order and the target angle are
  hidden from the player until the spin stops (outcome resolved by the
  launcher from the run-seeded RNG before launch).
- Code-first visuals only (`drawPowerUpIcon` / `drawWeaponIcon`); no external
  art assets.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/MiniBossWheelScene.ts` (new)
- `src/core/gameConfig.ts` (register the scene)
- `src/powerups/icons.ts` (reused unchanged)
- `src/scenes/MineralChoiceScene.ts` (pattern reference)
- `src/powerups/miniBossWheel.ts` (outcome resolution, consumed unchanged)
- `src/scenes/__tests__/MiniBossWheelScene.test.ts` (paired test item)

  wheel slot distribution and outcome resolver"

- Spinning is **player-initiated** (click/keyboard): the wheel animation starts fast and eases out (≈2.2 s total, at most one overshoot revolution, duration exported as a constant), the outcome is not predictable until it stops, and the landed wedge is highlighted and applied exactly once.

## Context

Part of **Mini-Boss rewards become valuable (AH-0MVLISU03006WDOD)**. The
paired implementation item for "Test the PlayScene wheel reward flow and
empty-owned fallback": this item makes those tests green.

## Summary

Rework `PlayScene.openMiniBossReward` / `selectMiniBossReward` so a mini-boss
defeat launches the wheel overlay with the owned permanent kinds, applies the
resolved outcome exactly once through the shared reward machinery, falls back
to the hold-full-style three-option choice when nothing permanent is owned,
and keeps the demo auto-spin. The unlock machinery is already removed (parent
AC5, sibling item).

## Design

- Open: build the owned-kind snapshot once from
  `resolvePlayerSlotState(this.player).ownedIds`
  (power-up kinds and weapon drops; permanent view). When empty →
  **fallback**: open the shared `MineralChoiceScene` with the hold-full-style
  three options (`createRandomChoiceStrategy` / `chooseOptions`), applied
  permanently — a mini-boss always pays out (AC4).
- When populated: resolve the wheel outcome once from the run-seeded RNG
  (`drawWheelOutcome`/`miniBossWheel`) and launch `MiniBossWheelScene` with the
  wedges, the outcome and a single result callback. Pause exactly like the
  hold-full choice; pass the frozen fire schedule for the reduced-volume ghost
  fire; rebase the beat clock on resume.
- Select/result: apply the outcome once via `applyWheelOutcome`
  (shared reward seam), close the overlay, resume play, reset the open flag —
  a repeated select is a no-op.
- Demo mode: pass `autoSpinMs: BOT_MINERAL_CHOICE_DELAY_MS` so the attract bot
  auto-spins from the run-seeded RNG and never stalls.
- Test getters (`getMiniBossRewardOptions`, `isMiniBossRewardOpen`) preserved
  or re-homed so the wheel-flow tests keep a stable surface.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` (rework `openMiniBossReward` /
  `selectMiniBossReward`; drop unlock state)
- `src/scenes/MiniBossWheelScene.ts` (launched overlay)
- `src/powerups/miniBossWheel.ts` (outcome resolution + application)
- `src/powerups/slots.ts` (`resolvePlayerSlotState` — owned kinds)

## Goal (user story)

As an agent relying on the automated test-failure triage pipeline, I want a full-suite run to be immune to a concurrent checkout of its own working tree, so that a mid-run `git checkout`/fast-forward can never mint a spurious critical `test-failure` work item from a state that never existed at any single commit.

## Problem (confirmed, with evidence)

A full-suite run in the **main checkout** fast-forwarded from `4d9daf0b` to `c1330ef3` 69 s into a 150 s run (main-checkout reflog `merge origin/dev: Fast-forward` at 22:56:43Z; run started 22:55:34Z). The run reported `CombatEffectVisuals.test.ts` as **41 tests / 6 failed** — i.e. it loaded the **post-checkout test file** against the **pre-checkout source module** (the shared integration worker had already transformed `CombatEffectVisuals.ts` for an earlier test file). The 6 failures were exactly the tests depending on the newly added `FORCE_FIELD_SPENT_*` constants. The triage bot then filed AH-0MVSPXLIN0000P1R (critical) for a state that never existed at any commit; the work was already correctly implemented and green.

Evidence: `.worklog/cache/bcf7b83c580b124c2498bf50efdc0baa/` (red, mixed state), vs `.worklog/cache/e13cbd7ab82128fb5d8c19f1aeb4da67/` (green, same tree).

## Why this matters

- Burns a critical triage item and an implement session on a non-existent defect (this one).
- A red cached entry keyed by a *transient* git state can also poison the dev-push gate / audit evidence for the run.
- The precondition is routine: `implement.py finish` fast-forwards the main checkout's parent branch after each push, while other agents are running suites in that same checkout.

## Implementation sketch (framework side — `.pi`/skill tooling, not game code)

1. Snapshot the resolved git state (HEAD + dirty content fingerprint) **before** the suite starts, and verify it is unchanged **after** the suite completes.
2. On mismatch, discard the result: do not cache it under either fingerprint and do not feed it to the triage helper — re-run instead (or report `state_changed_during_run` and exit non-green *without* filing test-failure items).
3. Prefer running mutating suites in a worktree, or take a read-only/shared lock that `implement.py`'s parent-branch fast-forward respects, so the fast-forward cannot land under a running suite.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A full-suite run whose checkout changes mid-run never files a `test-failure` work item for failures observed across the checkout boundary.
- Such a run is reported as `state_changed_during_run` (non-mutating, non-caching) rather than as a genuine failure.
- A run whose git state is stable before and after still caches and triages exactly as today (no behaviour change on the normal path).
- Regression test: a simulated mid-run HEAD/dirty-content change produces the new non-triaging outcome, and an unchanged state produces the existing outcome.

## References

- discovered-from: AH-0MVSPXLIN0000P1R (spurious critical `test-failure` item minted by this race).
- Related fix commit: `c1330ef3` (parent AH-0MVRDMG0N000Y03Z).
- Runner/cache code: `.pi` skill `test` (`run_tests.py`, `test_cache.py` `compute_git_state`) and `implement.py` `phase_finish` Step 5 (parent-branch fast-forward).
data.title: Test-harness: a mid-run checkout of the main checkout must not mint spurious critical test-failure items

# Clamped hold restore seam (MineralHold + GameState)

Implementation feature for AH-0MVSSSFXK005ZW8O (Restarted levels do not handle hold full correctly).

## Goal (user story)

As a developer, I want checkpoint restore to go through the shared hold model instead of writing raw counts around it, so the game and the gyms cannot diverge on overflow semantics and a restored hold can never be over-capacity.

## Context

`src/core/GameState.ts` exposes `minerals` as a plain pass-through to `MineralHold.store`, whose setter is unguarded (`this._store = value`). There is no seam that restores a hold defensively: the only write path is `collect()`, which is normal-play semantics (it *records* overflow, which is exactly what a restore must not do). `MineralHold.capacity` has a setter that also re-bases `_initialCapacity`, so applying a restored capacity through it would silently change what a later `reset()` returns to.

Producer decisions already recorded on the parent: restored over-capacity minerals are clamped into `[0, capacity]` with overflow cleared (Q2 = A); the restored capacity is the checkpoint's capacity (Q1 = A).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC2 — Restored hold never exceeds capacity and carries no phantom overflow** — a store at or above capacity restores to capacity with overflow 0.
- [ ] **AC1 — clamped restore seam on the shared hold model** — `MineralHold` gains a restore seam that clamps the store into `[0, capacity]`, clears the recorded overflow and accepts the restored capacity without re-basing the first-hold baseline (`reset()` after a restore still returns to the first-hold capacity).
- [ ] **AC3 — restore never writes around the hold model** — `GameState` exposes the same restore seam, so the resume path never writes minerals through the raw `minerals` setter, and `startGame()` keeps its fresh-run reset of store, overflow and capacity progression.
- [ ] **AC4 — invalid input is defended** — a negative or non-finite store restores as 0 and an invalid capacity keeps the existing capacity; `collect()` and `resolve()` normal-play contracts are unchanged and existing unit tests stay green.
- [ ] **AC5 — unit coverage** — tests cover the clamp, empty-surplus, invalid-input, reset-after-restore and growth-multiplier-preserved cases via the test skill.


## Minimal implementation

- Add `restore(options: { store?: number; capacity?: number })` (name/shape at the implementer's discretion) on `MineralHold`; set `_capacity` directly and clamp `_store`, leaving `_initialCapacity` untouched.
- Delegate from `GameState` (`restoreHold(...)`), mirroring the existing `addMinerals`/`resolveHold` delegation style and doc comments.
- Unit tests alongside the existing ones in `src/core/mineralHold.test.ts` (and the `GameState` test file if one exists), written before the implementation.

## Key Files

- `src/core/mineralHold.ts` — the shared hold model; add the clamped restore seam and its doc comment.
- `src/core/GameState.ts` — delegating `restoreHold` seam; `minerals`/`mineralCapacity` accessors unchanged.
- `src/core/mineralHold.test.ts` — unit tests for the seam.
- `src/core/rules.ts` — default first-hold capacity constants consumed by the model (no change expected).

## Notes

- No gym change: gyms re-initialise and reset the shared hold in `_initMineralLayer()` and have no checkpoint path, so the parity rule (AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1) is satisfied by keeping the fix in the shared model rather than in a scene copy.
- Depends on the regression-test item (test-first): the seam is what makes those tests pass.
data.title: Clamped hold restore seam (MineralHold + GameState)

# Checkpoint schema v2 persists hold capacity

Implementation feature for AH-0MVSSSFXK005ZW8O (Restarted levels do not handle hold full correctly).

## Goal (user story)

As a player continuing my run, I want the hold capacity I had earned at the checkpoint to come back with me, so Continue does not silently reset my earned hold progression (5/10/20/…) to the first hold.

## Context

`src/core/checkpointStore.ts` persists level, wave, lives, score, minerals, weapon/power-up levels, unlocked weapons and the run seed, but **not** the hold's capacity progression — `CHECKPOINT_VERSION` is 1 and `parseCheckpoint()` rebuilds a `Checkpoint` with no hold-capacity field. On resume the progression has already been reset to the first-hold capacity by `gameState.startGame()` + `mineralCapacity = rules.mineralHoldCapacity`, so the saved mineral count can exceed the resumed capacity.

Producer decision (Q1 = A, recorded in the parent Appendix): restore the capacity progression from the checkpoint; bump the schema version; legacy checkpoints without the field load and default to the first-hold capacity.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC3 — Resume restores the hold's capacity progression (producer decision Q1: A)** — `Checkpoint` persists the hold capacity and `_restoreCheckpoint()` applies it before the minerals, so the resumed run keeps the capacity it had earned at the checkpoint.
- [ ] **AC1 — schema version bumped** — the checkpoint carries a hold-capacity field and the schema version is bumped to 2; `saveCheckpoint()` writes the field.
- [ ] **AC2 — legacy checkpoints still load** — a version-1 payload with no capacity field loads and defaults to the first-hold capacity, rather than degrading to "no checkpoint".
- [ ] **AC4 — invalid values fall back, corrupt data still rejected** — a non-finite, negative, zero or non-numeric capacity falls back to the default; corrupt JSON still yields null and never throws; a round-trip preserves a non-default capacity such as 20.
- [ ] **AC5 — the save path writes the live capacity** — a mini-boss defeat persists the run's current hold capacity, asserted by extending the existing mini-boss checkpoint save test.
- [ ] **AC6 — Verification suite** — the new checkpoint tests and the full project suite pass via the test skill.


## Minimal implementation

- Extend the `Checkpoint` interface and `parseCheckpoint()` sanitisation; add the default constant import from `src/core/rules.ts` (or a local constant if importing rules into the store is undesirable — record the choice in a comment).
- Add `mineralHoldCapacity: this.gameState.mineralCapacity` to the `_saveCheckpoint()` payload.
- Tests in `src/core/checkpointStore.test.ts` (round-trip, legacy default, invalid fallback, corrupt JSON) plus the `PlayScene.test.ts` save assertion.

## Key Files

- `src/core/checkpointStore.ts` — payload interface, `CHECKPOINT_VERSION` bump, `parseCheckpoint()` legacy defaulting and validation.
- `src/core/checkpointStore.test.ts` — round-trip plus legacy/invalid fallback tests.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `_saveCheckpoint()` writes the current hold capacity.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` — mini-boss checkpoint save assertion extended.
- `src/core/rules.ts` — `DEFAULT_MINERAL_HOLD_CAPACITY` default used for legacy payloads.

## Notes

- Documented assumption: the legacy default is the **rules default constant** (5), not a customised `mineralHoldCapacity` tunable value. A legacy checkpoint therefore resumes at 5 even if the player had configured a different first-hold capacity; this matches the parent AC3 wording and keeps the store free of runtime rules coupling. Recorded in the parent plan notes.
- The version field is informational only today (`parseCheckpoint` stamps the current version); migration is decided by field presence, so a v1 payload with an accidental capacity field is still handled by the same validation path.
- Back-compatibility constraint: a checkpoint written by a newer build must not crash an older one — the store's defensive-parse discipline is preserved.
data.title: Checkpoint schema v2 persists hold capacity

# Resume applies hold capacity then clamps the store

Implementation feature for AH-0MVSSSFXK005ZW8O (Restarted levels do not handle hold full correctly).

## Goal (user story)

As a player continuing my run, I want the resumed hold to start at the capacity I had earned and to hold no more minerals than it can, so the first hold-full choice after Continue is the only one due and the HUD bar never shows more than 100%.

## Context

`PlayScene._restoreCheckpoint()` currently does `this.gameState.minerals = checkpoint.minerals` — a raw write through the unguarded `MineralHold.store` setter — and then `_syncMineralHud()`. Because `create()` has already reset the progression to the first-hold capacity, an over-capacity saved count restores an over-capacity hold: the next collected mineral opens a hold-full choice and banks the whole surplus as overflow, which `resolve()` clamps to the doubled capacity, so the *next* hold is already full — the reported immediate second hold-full.

This item wires the clamped-restore seam (sibling) and the persisted capacity (sibling) into the game's restore path, making the regression tests green.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Resume restores the hold's capacity progression before the minerals** — `_restoreCheckpoint()` applies the checkpoint's hold capacity first, then restores the store through the clamped `GameState.restoreHold(...)` seam, and re-syncs the HUD.
- [ ] **AC2 — No immediate second hold-full after Continue** — after resuming from an over-capacity checkpoint the hold is not full, minerals equal capacity, overflow is 0, and resolving the first hold-full leaves the next hold not full.
- [ ] **AC3 — HUD bar stays truthful on resume** — the hold bar's filled width is at most its total width after resume and the HUD counter shows the clamped value.
- [ ] **AC4 — Game↔gym parity preserved** — no gym gains checkpoint-resume behaviour; the equivalence guard and gym mineral tests still pass.
- [ ] **AC5 — a fresh run still resets the progression** — Play Game / New Game resets the hold to the first-hold capacity, so only the restore path changes.
- [ ] **AC6 — Verification suite** — the new regression tests fail on the current code and pass after the fix; the full project suite passes via the test skill.


## Minimal implementation

- In `_restoreCheckpoint()`, set the hold's capacity from the checkpoint and then restore the clamped store; keep the existing order (stats, seed, grant replay, lives last) and the existing `_syncMineralHud()` / `_refreshHudText()` calls.
- Update the `_restoreCheckpoint()` doc comment to state the resumed-hold semantics (capacity restored, store clamped, overflow cleared, first hold-full only after a real fill).
- No changes to `openMineralChoice()` / `selectMineralChoice()` / reward application.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `_restoreCheckpoint()` (capacity-then-clamped-store order) and its doc comment.
- `src/core/GameState.ts` — `restoreHold(...)` seam consumed by the restore path.
- `src/core/mineralHold.ts` — clamped restore seam consumed by `GameState`.
- `src/scenes/PlaySceneHUD.test.ts` — resume regression + HUD-bar assertions (from the test-first item).
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` — parity/duplicate-body guard that must stay green.
- `src/ui/HUD.ts` — verify only; no change expected once the store is capped.

## Notes

- Depends on both sibling implementation items (the seam and the persisted capacity).
- Keep the change inside the game's restore path; the shared hold model supplies the semantics so the gyms inherit nothing new.

# Wrap geometry primitives (test-first core)

Parent: **AH-0MVMISF0Q00314LG** — see "Bot should be aware of screen wrap around" (AH-0MVMISF0Q00314LG).

## Goal (user story)

As a **developer**, I want one shared, pure wrapped-geometry module that both the
enemy seam maths and the bot decision layer consume, so the bot's torus model
cannot drift from the one the game (and the wrap-aware enemies) already use, and
so every later wrap slice in this epic is a one-line call rather than a new copy
of the seam maths.

## Context

The enemy wrap epic (AH-0MV9G3DZ9003P7P8) already landed the primitives:

- `wrappedAxisDelta(from, to, size)` and `aimVectorToTarget(...)` in
  `src/scenes/core/enemyTargeting.ts`;
- `wrapPosition(x, y, world)` / `applyPostMotionWrap*` in
  `src/scenes/core/enemyWrap.ts`;
- `PLAYFIELD_WORLD` (`960 x 540`) in `src/scenes/core/enemyWrap.ts`.

Those live under `src/scenes/core/`, so the bot decision layer cannot consume them
without a `src/ai` → `src/scenes` dependency. The parent epic's constraint is
**one shared implementation** — no divergent per-behaviour seam copies — so the
primitives are promoted to a neutral module and the scene modules re-export them.

Two repo assertions constrain the move:

- `src/wrapAwareDocs.test.ts` asserts the docs mention `aimVectorToTarget` and
  `wrappedAxisDelta`, so those names must survive (re-export is enough).
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` proves game↔gym parity for
  the wrap maths; its imports must keep working.

## Scope

Used by later slices: wrapped bearing/delta, wrapped distance, near-tie
hysteresis (so a nearly-equal raw vs. wrapped path does not flip duplicates every
tick — a named risk on the parent), and a warm-2D-delta helper.

Preferred approach:

1. `src/utils/wrapGeometry.ts` — neutral, pure, no Phaser/scene import. Holds
   `WrapWorld`, `wrapAxis`, `wrapPosition`, `wrappedAxisDelta`, `wrappedDelta`,
   `wrappedDistance`, `wrappedBearing`, and the near-tie tie-break/hysteresis
   helper. `src/utils/` is already the neutral home for `movementModel.ts`, whose
   four-edge wrap is the model the bot must match.
2. `src/scenes/core/enemyTargeting.ts` and `src/scenes/core/enemyWrap.ts`
   re-export the moved symbols (`export { wrappedAxisDelta } from
   '../../utils/wrapGeometry'` style) and keep `PLAYFIELD_WORLD`, so
   `Scout.ts`, the equivalence suite and the docs assertions keep working
   unchanged.
3. `src/ai/framework/wrapGeometry.ts` — thin bot-facing re-export/binding of the
   same functions with the bot's `playfieldWidth`/`playfieldHeight` convenience
   wrappers (`wrappedDeltaToPlayer(player, point, t)` style), **delegating** to
   `src/utils/wrapGeometry.ts`. No second implementation body.
4. Unit tests written **first** (red → green): a dedicated
   `wrapGeometry.test.ts` module.

Fallback (only if the promotion turns out to be materially riskier than expected,
e.g. the equivalence guard or the docs assertion resists it): keep the primitives
where they are and have `src/ai/framework/wrapGeometry.ts` import them from
`src/scenes/core/`, recording the direction-of-dependency reason in a code
comment. The requirement is one implementation, not one file.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A single shared wrap-geometry implementation exists and is imported (not
   copied) by both the enemy seam modules and the new bot-side module; `git grep`
   shows exactly one definition of `wrappedAxisDelta`, `wrapPosition` and
   `wrapAxis` in `src/`, and the scene modules re-export rather than redefine.
2. `wrappedDelta(from, to, world)` returns the shortest signed 2-D delta and
   `wrappedDistance(from, to, world)` its magnitude; both reduce to the raw
   Euclidean values when the raw path is already the shortest one.
3. `wrappedBearing(from, to, world)` returns the unit vector along the shortest
   wrapped path; the raw-line case is bit-identical to today's
   `normalise(to - from)`.
4. Near-tie hysteresis: when the raw and wrapped route lengths differ by less
   than the tolerance, the helper keeps the caller's previous choice (or the raw
   route when no previous choice is supplied) so targeting cannot flip
   duplicates tick-to-tick; a route that is genuinely shorter by more than the
   tolerance is always taken.
5. Boundary semantics match the existing enemy seam exactly: an exact half-axis
   delta is a tie that keeps the direct delta; multi-period and out-of-range
   coordinates wrap by modulo; a non-positive/non-finite size or coordinate is
   passed through unchanged rather than producing `NaN`.
6. Unit tests (`src/utils/wrapGeometry.test.ts` and the bot-side
   `src/ai/framework/wrapGeometry.test.ts`) cover all four edges, both axes, the
   exact-half tie, multi-period overshoot, the no-wrap-model pass-through and the
   hysteresis case; existing `enemyWrap.test.ts`, `enemyTargeting` consumers,
   `wrapAwareDocs.test.ts` and `CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` stay green.
7. The changed-scope test gate passes via `/skill:test` (build → test → commit
   order) and the tests are written before the implementation.

## Key Files

- `src/utils/wrapGeometry.ts` (new) — promoted primitives and hysteresis helper.
- `src/utils/wrapGeometry.test.ts` (new) — test-first unit coverage.
- `src/ai/framework/wrapGeometry.ts` (new) — bot-facing delegation/binding.
- `src/ai/framework/wrapGeometry.test.ts` (new).
- `src/scenes/core/enemyTargeting.ts`, `src/scenes/core/enemyWrap.ts` — re-export.
- `src/wrapAwareDocs.test.ts`, `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` —
  must stay green.

## Dependencies

None. This is the foundation that blocks every other child of
AH-0MVMISF0Q00314LG's wrap work.

# Wrap-aware steering and clearance

Parent: "Bot should be aware of screen wrap around" (AH-0MVMISF0Q00314LG) — AC1.

## Goal (user story)

As a **player watching the attract demo**, I want the bot to cross a screen edge
to reach a target that is closer the other way, instead of treating the four
seam edges as walls it must not approach, so its movement looks like a human's
and it stops camping near walls it wrongly fears.

## Context

Both steering evaluators reject a bearing purely because it reaches an edge
inside `wallMargin`:

- legacy `evaluateVector` — `src/ai/botDecision.ts` ("reaches a wall within
  `wallMargin`", `wallMargin: 40` default);
- competent `evaluateDirection` — `src/ai/framework/competent/steering.ts`
  ("Walls: reject a bearing that reaches an edge inside the wall margin",
  `wallMargin: 30` default).

Both also derive the objective bearing from the raw straight line, so a
seam-crossing route to an objective is never even considered. The playfield
genuinely wraps: the player ship wraps at all four edges
(`src/utils/movementModel.ts`), bullets wrap (`src/scenes/core/bulletLifecycle.ts`),
and wrap-aware enemies now fly over the edges too (AH-0MV9G3DZ9003P7P8).

This slice consumes the primitives from the wrap-geometry child
(AH-0MVMISF0Q00314LG's wrap-geometry primitive child) — no seam maths is written
here.

## Scope

1. Remove the wall test from both evaluators: an edge is no longer a hazard, so
   `evaluateVector`/`evaluateDirection` never mark a bearing unsafe merely for
   reaching an edge. Keep clearance meaningful: the distance-to-edge term stays
   only as a *clearance* contribution if it is still useful, and if it is dropped
   the clearance cap semantics are preserved.
2. Steering objectives use the **shortest wrapped path**: the objective bearing
   fed to the fan is computed with the wrapped delta (raw vs. seam-crossing
   duplicate of the objective, whichever is shorter), with the near-tie
   hysteresis from the geometry child so the chosen duplicate does not flip
   every tick.
3. Edge-crossing motion is used deliberately when net-positive (Q2 in the
   parent Appendix) — it falls out of shortest-path selection; no scripted wrap
   manœuvre and no change to the human-like governor
   (`src/ai/botHumanLike.ts`).
4. Update the existing integration assertion in
   `src/ai/botSteering.integration.test.ts` that presumes the bot "never wraps
   the screen" (the brake-to-stop case) so it still asserts a controlled stop
   without asserting the bot cannot cross a seam; add seam scenarios instead.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The four arena edges stop being walls in the steering safety/clearance test:
   neither the legacy `evaluateVector` (`src/ai/botDecision.ts`) nor the
   competent `evaluateDirection` (`src/ai/framework/competent/steering.ts`)
   rejects a direction solely because it reaches an edge within `wallMargin`; a
   unit test per evaluator drives a bearing straight at each of the four edges
   from mid-playfield and asserts `safe === true`.
2. Steering toward an objective uses the shortest wrapped path: when the
   seam-crossing route to the objective is shorter than the raw line, the chosen
   bearing points at the wrapped duplicate; when the raw line is already
   shortest, the chosen bearing is unchanged from today's behaviour.
3. Unit tests cover **each of the four edges** (left/right/top/bottom): the
   wrapped bearing is chosen when it is shorter, and an edge-crossing direction
   is safe when it does not otherwise threaten.
4. Hysteresis at nearly-equal raw/wrapped paths: a test drives a sequence of
   ticks where the two route lengths swap by a tiny margin each tick and asserts
   the committed objective duplicate does not oscillate.
5. The human-like governor's reaction cadence, W/A/D control mapping and human
   thrust presses are unchanged; existing steering/bot integration tests stay
   green apart from the deliberately updated "never wraps" assertion, which is
   re-stated as "still brakes to a controlled stop".
6. The changed-scope test gate passes via `/skill:test` (build → test → commit
   order) with tests written first.

## Key Files

- `src/ai/framework/competent/steering.ts` — `evaluateDirection`, `bearingTo`,
  `chooseSteeringDirection`.
- `src/ai/botDecision.ts` — `evaluateVector` and the legacy target-bearing path.
- `src/ai/framework/competent/steering.test.ts`,
  `src/ai/botDecision.test.ts` — per-edge wrap tests (written first).
- `src/ai/botSteering.integration.test.ts` — updated "never wraps" assertion plus
  seam-crossing scenarios.
- `src/ai/framework/competent/competentBot.integration.test.ts` — wrap scenario.

## Dependencies

Blocked by the wrap-geometry primitives child (shared wrapped delta/bearing +
hysteresis must exist first).

## Out of scope

`wallMargin` removal from tunables, style fitting and the tuning UI (separate
child); aim/intercept, nearest-selection, threat prediction and eval parity
(separate children).

# Seam-aware aim and intercept

Parent: "Bot should be aware of screen wrap around" (AH-0MVMISF0Q00314LG) — AC2
(aim half).

## Goal (user story)

As a **player**, I want the demo bot to aim and fire at an enemy along the
shortest wrapped path — including off one edge to arrive from the opposite edge
— so engagements play out across the whole wrap-around arena.

## Context

Aim maths is raw Euclidean today:

- `bearingTo` (`src/ai/framework/competent/steering.ts`) — `normalise(to - from)`;
- `interceptPoint` (same module) — lead solve on raw deltas;
- the legacy aim/aim-delta path in `src/ai/botDecision.ts` — `atan2` on raw
  deltas.

The enemy side already aims on the torus via `aimVectorToTarget` /
`wrappedAxisDelta` (`src/scenes/core/enemyTargeting.ts`, used by
`Scout.tryFireAimedBullet`), so the bot currently fights a wrap-aware opponent
with a wrap-blind gun — a systematic disadvantage once enemy wrap lands.

## Scope

1. `bearingTo` and `interceptPoint` compute their deltas along the shortest
   wrapped path (per-axis wrapped delta), with the bot's
   `playfieldWidth`/`playfieldHeight`; both accept the wrap model without
   changing their existing signatures' call sites more than necessary (a
   `WrapWorld`/tunables argument).
2. The intercept solve predicts the target on the torus: the predicted point is
   the target's position advanced by its velocity, then the *route* to it is the
   shortest wrapped one, so a lead solution that must cross a seam is still
   produced. Stationary targets reduce exactly to the wrapped bearing.
3. Legacy aim in `src/ai/botDecision.ts` uses the same shared wrapped maths
   (delegating to the shared module, no second implementation).
4. Behaviour is bit-identical when the raw line is already the shortest path.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Seam-aware aim and targeting — aim and target selection run on the torus: `bearingTo`/`interceptPoint` and the legacy aim compute deltas along the shortest wrapped path.
2. Aim runs on the torus: `bearingTo` and `interceptPoint`
   (`src/ai/framework/competent/steering.ts`) and the legacy aim compute in
   `src/ai/botDecision.ts` compute deltas along the shortest wrapped path, using
   the shared wrap-geometry primitives (no copied seam maths).
3. When the wrapped route to a target is shorter than the raw line, the returned
   aim angle equals the wrapped-path angle (test asserts the exact expected
   heading for a target across each of the four edges); firing off one edge
   arrives from the opposite edge.
4. When the raw line is already shortest, the aim angle is unchanged from the
   pre-change behaviour (regression test on a representative non-seam geometry).
5. `interceptPoint` leads a moving target across the seam: a test with a target
   whose velocity carries it over an edge returns the wrapped intercept point and
   converges (iteration count honoured), while a stationary target reduces to the
   wrapped bearing.
6. The legacy decision layer's aim output is byte-for-byte the pre-change value
   for a non-seam geometry (golden assertion in `src/ai/botDecision.test.ts`).
7. The changed-scope test gate passes via `/skill:test` (build → test → commit
   order) with tests written first.

# Wrapped nearest-selection and behaviour distances

Parent: "Bot should be aware of screen wrap around" (AH-0MVMISF0Q00314LG) — AC2
(targeting half).

## Goal (user story)

As a **player**, I want the demo bot to pick and pursue the target that is
genuinely nearest on the torus — and to flee across a seam when that is the
safest separation — so its choices match what a human sees on a wrap-around
arena.

## Context

Every nearest/threshold decision in the competent layer is raw Euclidean:

- `nearestTarget` and `bestWeightedTarget` (`src/ai/framework/competent/goals.ts`)
  — `Math.hypot(point - player)`;
- goal-range gates (boss range, proximity falloff) in the same module;
- `nearestEnemyDistance` and `nearestDistance` helper
  (`src/ai/framework/worldModel.ts`);
- collect/engage/evade distances and the evade flee vector
  (`src/ai/framework/competent/behaviours.ts`), including the
  `repositionRadius`/`longTravelDistance` comparisons;
- the legacy decision layer's distance/closest-approach uses in
  `src/ai/botDecision.ts`.

Consequence today: a mineral one pixel past the right edge is scored as ~940 px
away, a pursuing enemy across the seam is ignored, and `evade` computes a flee
vector that runs *into* the seam instead of away along it.

## Scope

1. Wrapped distance for target selection: `nearestTarget`, `bestWeightedTarget`,
   the boss/enemy proximity gates, `nearestEnemyDistance`/`nearestDistance` and
   the collect/engage/evade distance thresholds all measure wrapped distance.
2. The returned *point* is the target itself (unchanged identity — the caller
   still aims at the entity); only the measured distance is wrapped, so nothing
   downstream needs a "duplicate" concept for targeting.
3. Objectives derived from a target use the wrapped delta (the geometry child's
   helper), so `collect`/`engage` steer across the seam when that is shorter.
4. `evade` flees across a seam when the wrapped separation is the safest/nearest
   escape: the weighted flee vector is computed from wrapped deltas, so fleeing
   away from a shot that arrived across a seam works.
5. Behaviour is unchanged where raw and wrapped agree (regression tests).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Wrapped nearest-selection: `nearestTarget`, `bestWeightedTarget`,
   `nearestEnemyDistance` and the collect/engage/evade distance thresholds
   (`src/ai/framework/competent/goals.ts`,
   `src/ai/framework/worldModel.ts`,
   `src/ai/framework/competent/behaviours.ts`) choose nearest by wrapped
   distance, using the shared wrap-geometry primitives.
2. A test where the raw and wrapped ordering **differ** asserts the wrapped-nearest
   candidate wins (two minerals placed so the seam-crossing one is nearer), on
   both axes, while a same-side pair keeps today's choice.
3. When the wrapped route to an enemy, boss or mineral is shorter than the raw
   line, the derived objective bearing points at the seam duplicate (asserted on
   the chosen intent direction); when the raw line is shortest the intent is
   unchanged.
4. `evade` produces a flee direction pointing away from a shot across the seam:
   a test with a threatening shot near the opposite edge asserts the intent
   increases wrapped separation rather than decreasing it.
5. The `.distance` values returned alongside targets are the wrapped distances (a
   direct assertion), so downstream thresholds (`engageRange`, `collectRange`,
   `repositionRadius`, `longTravelDistance`) compare consistently.
6. The changed-scope test gate passes via `/skill:test` (build → test → commit
   order) with tests written first.

## Key Files

- `src/ai/framework/competent/goals.ts` — `nearestTarget`, `bestWeightedTarget`,
  proximity/range gates.
- `src/ai/framework/worldModel.ts` — `nearestEnemyDistance`, `nearestDistance`.
- `src/ai/framework/competent/behaviours.ts` — collect/engage/evade distances,
  evade flee vector, reposition.
- `src/ai/framework/competent/goals.test.ts`,
  `src/ai/framework/worldModel.test.ts`,
  `src/ai/framework/competent/behaviours.test.ts` — wrap cases (written first).

## Dependencies

Blocked by the wrap-geometry primitives child.

# Seam-aware threat and hazard prediction

Parent: "Bot should be aware of screen wrap around" (AH-0MVMISF0Q00314LG) — AC3.

## Goal (user story)

As a **player**, I want the demo bot to dodge a shot that is about to arrive
across the seam, so it survives what any human sees coming — now that wrap-aware
enemies fire across seams (AH-0MV9G3DZ9003P7P8).

## Context

Threat prediction is raw Euclidean:

- `predictIncomingFire` and `classifyShot` (`src/ai/framework/worldModel.ts`) —
  relative position/velocity of the shot vs. the player, closest approach on the
  raw line; the fire-tell estimate is a straight line from the enemy to the
  player's raw position;
- the competent `closestApproach` solve
  (`src/ai/framework/competent/steering.ts`) used by `evaluateDirection` for
  hazards and incoming fire, and by `hazardThreatensPlayer` / the engage kiting
  gate;
- the legacy path-crossing checks in `src/ai/botDecision.ts`
  (`evaluateVector`'s bullet and fire-tell solves);
- `hazardVelocity` (`src/ai/framework/hazardVelocity.ts`) already clamps
  spurious position jumps (`HAZARD_MAX_ESTIMATED_SPEED = 900`) to filter
  wrap-around/respawn teleports.

Consequence: a bullet that will arrive from the opposite edge is predicted on a
line that starts ~900 px away in the wrong direction, so the bot stands still
and dies to it.

## Scope

1. Wrap the *relative* geometry of the prediction: the shot-to-player separation
   is the shortest wrapped delta (per axis), so closest approach and time-to-
   closest are computed on the torus. Where wrapping changes the problem, the
   predicted approach is taken along the wrapped route.
2. Compute the wrapped route for both in-flight bullets and fire-tell estimates
   (`predictIncomingFire`'s `assumedBulletSpeed` line) so a tell that will fire
   across the seam is classified as threatening.
3. Run the competent `closestApproach` (hazards and incoming fire) and the legacy
   path-crossing solves on the wrapped deltas, sharing one implementation.
4. Re-verify `hazardVelocity`'s clamp: with positions modelled on the torus the
   tracker must still clamp only true teleports/respawns and must not swallow a
   legitimate seam re-entry (which is a real ~width-sized jump in raw
   coordinates). Prefer wrapping the *delta* used to estimate velocity over
   raising the clamp; if a change is needed, cover it with tests proving a seam
   crossing yields the hazard's true velocity and a respawn still yields zero/its
   previous estimate.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Seam-aware threat and hazard prediction: `predictIncomingFire` runs on the wrapped torus.
2. `predictIncomingFire` (`src/ai/framework/worldModel.ts`), the competent
   `closestApproach` solves and the legacy path-crossing checks
   (`src/ai/framework/competent/steering.ts`, `src/ai/botDecision.ts`) operate on
   the wrapped torus, using the shared wrap-geometry primitives.
3. A seam-crossing shot is classified as threatening: a test places an enemy
   bullet just outside one edge travelling inward so its wrapped path crosses the
   player, and asserts `threatens === true` and a small `closestDistance` /
   `timeToClosest` — a raw-line-only view would miss it (assert the raw view
   would give a large distance in the same test as a comment/assertion).
4. A shot on the player's own side of the seam is classified exactly as before
   today's behaviour (regression assertion on distance/time/threatens).
5. The `hazardVelocity` tracker's wrap-jump clamp is re-verified and tested: a
   hazard that crosses a seam between decision ticks yields its true (small)
   velocity rather than a clamped/absurd one, and a genuine respawn/teleport is
   still clamped — so the tracker never double-compensates under the torus model.
6. `evaluateDirection` rejects an unsafe bearing when a seam-crossing shot is
   predicted to intersect it, and `hazardThreatensPlayer` reports a seam-crossing
   hazard as threatening.
7. The changed-scope test gate passes via `/skill:test` (build → test → commit
   order) with tests written first.
##

# Retire the wallMargin tunable

Parent: "Bot should be aware of screen wrap around" (AH-0MVMISF0Q00314LG) — AC4.

## Goal (user story)

As a **developer**, I want the now-meaningless `wallMargin` knob retired cleanly
across the decision layer, style fitting, the tuning UI and saved configs, so
there is no dead tunable suggesting the arena has walls and no saved bot tuning
fails to load.

## Context

`wallMargin` exists only to express "the edges are walls", which the
wrap-aware-steering child removes. Current consumers:

- `src/ai/botDecision.ts` — `BotDecisionTunables.wallMargin` and the default
  (`40`), plus the `evaluateVector` wall test;
- `src/ai/framework/competent/tunables.ts` — `CompetentBotTunables.wallMargin`
  and the default (`30`);
- `src/ai/style/fitting.ts` — `clamp(t.wallMargin, 6, 90)`, the
  `WALL_MARGIN_CAUTIOUS`/`WALL_MARGIN_RISKY` lerp into the fitted tunables, and
  the `knob: 'wallMargin'` style-fit mapping entry;
- `src/ai/tuningFields.ts` — the `competent`-group field descriptor;
- `src/data/bot-tuning.json` — a saved `"wallMargin": 120` value;
- tests: `src/ai/botDecision.test.ts` (tunable-keys assertion, wall case),
  `src/ai/style/fitting.test.ts`, `src/ai/style/evaluation.test.ts`.

## Scope

1. Delete `wallMargin` from both tunable interfaces, defaults, the tuning-field
   descriptor, the style-fit lerp/mapping and the saved
   `src/data/bot-tuning.json`.
2. Keep **unknown-field tolerance**: loading a saved tuning that still contains
   `wallMargin` must not fail or warn fatally — a test loads a config containing
   the retired field (as the shipped `bot-tuning.json` did) and asserts the bot
   still starts with the remaining tunables applied. If the load path currently
   rejects unknown keys, add tolerant handling rather than a migration script.
3. Update the style-fit mapping documentation in `src/ai/style/fitting.ts`'s
   header table (the "risk appetite" row must no longer claim `wallMargin`) and
   the tunable docs in `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md` that describe it.
4. Record the behaviour change for old configs (the field is ignored) in the
   work-item comment and, where the tuning UI lists fields, in the UI docs.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `wallMargin` retired cleanly: the now-meaningless wall-margin tunable is retired across botDecision.ts, competent/tunables.ts, style/fitting.ts and tuningFields.ts.
2. `wallMargin` is retired across `src/ai/botDecision.ts`,
   `src/ai/framework/competent/tunables.ts`, `src/ai/style/fitting.ts`,
   `src/ai/tuningFields.ts` and `src/data/bot-tuning.json`; `git grep -i
   wallmargin src/` returns no live tunable reference (historical comments may
   only explain the retirement).
3. Saved bot-tuning configs still load with the field gone: a test loads a
   config object (and `src/data/bot-tuning.json`) that either omits the field or
   still carries it, and asserts the bot starts, the remaining tunables are
   applied, and no fatal error/warning is raised.
4. The style-fit mapping is updated: `src/ai/style/fitting.ts` no longer emits a
   `wallMargin` knob entry and `src/ai/style/fitting.test.ts` asserts the retired
   field is absent from fitted tunables and from the knob list, with the
   remaining risk-appetite knobs still fitted (existing assertions that reference
   `wallMargin` are updated, not deleted wholesale).
5. The tuning UI/docs no longer advertise the knob: `src/ai/tuningFields.ts` has
   no descriptor, and the `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md` tunable table/description is
   updated (a docs test asserting the retired field's absence is added).
6. Behaviour equivalence: with a wrap-aware steering model the removed wall test
   changes nothing about hazard-avoidance decisions; the steering unit suite
   stays green with the field gone.
7. The changed-scope test gate passes via `/skill:test` (build → test → commit
   order) with tests written first.

# Eval arena wrap parity

Parent: "Bot should be aware of screen wrap around" (AH-0MVMISF0Q00314LG) — AC5.

## Goal (user story)

As a **developer**, I want the headless eval arena to mirror the shipped
wrap-around world, so wrap-aware play actually earns eval credit and eval scores
measure the same physics the bot faces in the game.

## Context

The headless arena (`src/ai/eval/arena.ts`) diverges from the game in two ways:

- **Bullets are culled off-field** — `offField(point, width, height)` with
  `BULLET_MARGIN` retires player and enemy bullets once they leave the playfield,
  whereas the game wraps both (`src/scenes/core/bulletLifecycle.ts`, four-edge
  wrap, AH-0MU960UTE001PTV0).
- **Hostile fire aims at the raw player position** — the enemy bullet is launched
  with `dx = player.x - hostile.x` on the raw line, so no hostile shot ever
  crosses a seam, even though wrap-aware enemies now fire along the shortest
  wrapped path.

Consequence: a wrap-aware bot is scored in a world where the seam does not exist
for bullets, so the epic's behaviour earns no credit and eval-driven tuning is
misleading.

## Scope

1. Wrap player and enemy bullets at the four edges each tick (position-only
   modulo on the playfield period, matching
   `src/utils/movementModel.ts`/`bulletLifecycle.ts`), retiring the off-field
   cull for bullets that are alive by lifetime. Bullet lifetime/expiry semantics
   are preserved.
2. Aim hostile fire along the shortest wrapped path using the shared seam maths
   (`aimVectorToTarget`, `wrapAware: true`) so eval hostile fire matches the
   wrap-aware enemy fire in the game — no copy of the aim maths in
   `src/ai/eval/`.
3. Keep everything else about the arena unchanged (drops, minerals, hit radii,
   metrics), so scores stay comparable; document the parity change in
   `docs/EVALUATION.md` (the fuller docs pass lives in the docs child, but this
   note is required here).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The headless eval arena (`src/ai/eval/arena.ts`) is at wrap-parity with the
   game: enemy bullets wrap at the edges instead of being culled off-field, and
   player bullets do too (matching the game's bullet wrap model), while bullet
   lifetime expiry is preserved.
2. Hostile fire aims along the shortest wrapped path (shared
   `aimVectorToTarget`/wrapped-delta maths, no duplicate implementation), so an
   enemy near one edge fires at a player near the opposite edge across the seam.
3. `src/ai/eval/arena.test.ts` covers the wrapped-bullet case (a bullet crossing
   each edge reappears on the opposite side and is not culled) and the seam-aim
   case (a hostile's launched bullet heading equals the wrapped-path heading),
   plus a regression case proving a same-side shot is unchanged.
4. Eval metrics capture wrap-aware play: a test (or the existing metric
   assertions) shows a bullet that crossed the seam is still counted as a
   live/hittable projectile rather than being retired, so avoidable-hit and
   damage metrics are computed on the wrapped world.
5. `docs/EVALUATION.md` documents the wrap parity (bullets wrap, hostile fire is
   seam-aware) and any metric interpretation change.
6. The full eval suite (`src/ai/eval/*.test.ts`) stays green and the changed-scope
   test gate passes via `/skill:test` (build → test → commit order) with tests
   written first.

## Key Files

- `src/ai/eval/arena.ts` — bullet stepping/retirement, hostile fire launch.
- `src/ai/eval/arena.test.ts` — wrapped-bullet and seam-aim cases (written first).
- `docs/EVALUATION.md` — wrap-parity note.

## Dependencies

Blocked by the wrap-geometry primitives child and the seam-aware aim child
(shared wrapped aim maths).

# Wrap docs and full validation sweep

Parent: "Bot should be aware of screen wrap around" (AH-0MVMISF0Q00314LG) — AC6.

## Goal (user story)

As a **developer**, I want the bot framework and evaluation docs to describe the
wrap-aware (torus) model, and a wrap-scenario validation sweep that proves the
human-like feel is preserved, so the next person changing bot behaviour knows the
model and can trust the suite.

## Context

The decision layer's documented model will have changed substantially: edges are
no longer walls, geometry is wrapped, `wallMargin` is gone and eval is
wrap-parity. `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md` and `docs/EVALUATION.md` currently describe
the pre-wrap model, and repo docs are asserted by tests
(`src/ai/framework/botFrameworkDocs.test.ts`,
`src/ai/framework/competent/competentBotDocs.test.ts`,
`src/ai/eval/evaluationDocs.test.ts`, `src/wrapAwareDocs.test.ts`).

## Scope

1. `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md` — document the single wrap-aware model: the shared
   wrap-geometry helpers and where they live, wrapped steering/aim/nearest/
   threat prediction, the near-tie hysteresis, the retired `wallMargin`, and the
   preserved human-like governor (reaction cadence, W/A/D, thrust feel).
2. `docs/EVALUATION.md` — document eval wrap parity (wrapped bullets, seam-aware
   hostile aim) and what it means for score comparison.
3. Wrap-scenario tests that exercise the whole stack end-to-end (not just unit
   level): a competent-bot integration scenario where the shortest route to a
   target is across a seam (bot crosses and reaches it), and a survival scenario
   where a seam-arriving shot is dodged; the human-like governor's cadence/controls
   assertions stay green.
4. Full-suite validation: the changed-scope gate first, then the dev-push gate's
   full suite (never run ad hoc — always via `/skill:test`).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Unit/integration tests cover wrapped steering (all four edges, raw vs.
   wrapped), seam aim, seam threat prediction, wrapped nearest-selection where raw
   and wrapped ordering differ, wall-margin retirement and eval parity — each
   traced to the child that added it, with the docs child adding the end-to-end
   scenarios rather than duplicating unit coverage.
2. The human-like governor's reaction cadence, controls and thrust feel are
   unchanged: existing steering/bot integration tests stay green, plus new wrap
   scenarios (`src/ai/framework/competent/competentBot.integration.test.ts`,
   `src/ai/botSteering.integration.test.ts`) that assert the bot crosses a seam
   for a nearer target and dodges a seam-arriving shot.
3. `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md` and `docs/EVALUATION.md` describe the wrap-aware model
   (shared helpers, wrapped steering/aim/nearest/threat, hysteresis, retired
   `wallMargin`, eval parity), and the docs-assertion tests
   (`botFrameworkDocs.test.ts` and the eval docs tests) are updated and green.
4. The full project test suite passes via `/skill:test` with the new changes; no
   ad-hoc test invocation is used.
5. Any divergence discovered (behaviour deliberately left wrap-blind, or a gym/game
   parity caveat) is recorded in the work-item comment and, where non-obvious, a
   code comment next to the divergence.

## Key Files

- `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md`, `docs/EVALUATION.md`.
- `src/ai/framework/botFrameworkDocs.test.ts`,
  `src/ai/framework/competent/competentBotDocs.test.ts`,
  `src/ai/eval/evaluationDocs.test.ts`, `src/wrapAwareDocs.test.ts`.
- `src/ai/framework/competent/competentBot.integration.test.ts`,
  `src/ai/botSteering.integration.test.ts`.

## Dependencies

Blocked by every other child of this epic (steering, aim, nearest-selection,
threat prediction, wallMargin retirement, eval parity) — it documents and
validates their combined result.

# Multi-scene capture breaks mid-sequence: `window.__aiHellFade` lost, recording salvaged

Blocking defect discovered while verifying the scripted-video arc (parent AH-0MVPJ3NSK008V5VB, parent AC3; child F6 AH-0MVRMFVQ6007IC4D). The seven-scene arc cannot currently be recorded end-to-end, so none of the three scripted pay-offs (Hull Full, mini-boss death, boss death) can be verified on camera.

## Observed behaviour

Running the documented command at dev `d70cc3e2` (config committed by F6):

```
npm run capture:scenes -- --config examples/scenes.json --json
```

fails after scene 4:

```
[capture] Scene 1/7: GymLevel (play 2.0s, capture 8.0s)
[capture] Scene 2/7: GymLevel (play 2.0s, capture 9.0s)
[capture] Scene 3/7: GymLevel (play 2.0s, capture 7.0s)
[capture] Scene 4/7: GymLevel (play 2.0s, capture 7.0s)
[capture] Clip 1/1 failed: page.evaluate: TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'fadeTo')
Capture failed ... salvaged 8746297 B (8.34 MiB) of streamed video at
  capture-output/scenes-2026-10-29T10-27-12-041Z.partial.webm
```

Exit code is non-zero and no finished `.webm` is produced (only `*.partial.webm`, 754 video frames ≈ 39 s of the planned 73 s).

`fadeTo` lives on the page global `window.__aiHellFade`, installed once by `installCaptureComposite` (`scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs`, ~line 1271) and called per transition by `driveSceneSequence` (~line 2476). The overlay is installed successfully at start ("Capture overlay installed (canvas mirror + 0.25 s fades)"), and the fades after scenes 1-3 work; the global is gone by the fade after scene 4.

## Prior evidence (F6 session, 2026-10-29 05:21-06:00)

- Two full 73 s recordings were produced, but in the recorded sequence the **main boss took no damage at all** (bar fill matched `bossHitsRemaining` = 1/200 for 20+ s), while a standalone Playwright probe with the same launch args and the same setup killed the boss at ~6.6-6.9 s.
- The session was still root-causing when it was killed by a provider outage; the config it had been tuning (`bossHitsRemaining: 1`, weapon swaps) was then committed by the `implement.py finish` path without on-camera verification.

## Hypothesis (to confirm)

A **page reload** (or document swap) occurs mid-sequence and wipes both the page-side capture globals and the single `MediaRecorder`. Likely trigger: the Vite dev server used by the capture (`runCaptureSession`, `logLevel: 'warn'`) re-optimising dependencies / triggering a reload when a lazily-imported gym module (e.g. the mini-boss/boss scene module loaded by `startScene` -> `discoverPageGymScenes`) pulls in a dependency not yet in the optimised set. Alternative: renderer reload on scene switch or a `page` navigation caused by the gym scene boot path.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Root cause identified.** The mid-sequence loss of `window.__aiHellFade` (and the reason the recorded boss never takes damage) is diagnosed and recorded as a comment with concrete evidence (navigation/console log, Vite reload message, or equivalent).
- **AC2 — Fix.** `npm run capture:scenes -- --config examples/scenes.json --json` on a clean dev checkout completes successfully: exit code 0, one finished `.webm`, seven scenes in the payload, all fade probes passing, total runtime ≈70-75 s.
- **AC3 — Pay-offs verifiable.** The recorded clip shows the three scripted pay-offs in their own scene windows (Hull Full resolution, mini-boss death, boss death), with the evidence (payload timings plus frame/probe data) recorded as a comment.
- **AC4 — No production surface change.** The fix stays in capture/dev tooling (`scripts/`, dev-gated `src/core/captureDirector.ts`); `npm run check-bundle` stays green and no shipped gameplay behaviour changes.
- **AC5 — Regression coverage.** A hermetic test pins the failure mode (e.g. the capture session detecting a page navigation/document swap during a multi-scene run and failing loudly with an actionable message, or the dev server configured so reloads cannot occur mid-run) — a test that fails without the fix.
- **AC6 — Docs.** `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md` records any new behaviour/limitation (e.g. reload suppression) where relevant.
